Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in 5xx + latency from us-west-2 (AZ-3) — Need immediate diversion play

Short update — I executed a targeted policy to de-prioritize AZ-3 for CloudFin's customer route and nudged requests to other AZs in us-west-2 and eastus. Change went out at 09:24 UTC.

What I changed:
- Router policy: applied per-customer override to reduce weight to AZ-3 to 5%
- Canary fallback: enabled eastus model-variant (same family, slightly older quantization) as fallback for requests that see retry throttle
- KV cache: persisted primary prefixes into eastus to reduce cold-starts

Immediate results: 503 rate dropped from 7% to ~1.1% within the first 4 minutes; p95 latency improved to ~350–400ms. CloudFin is still seeing occasional retries but overall much better.

We're rolling telemetry and continuing to observe. I also uploaded a short step-by-step to the runbook and attached it here.

SRE — Serving Runtime

Subject: Incident follow-up: evacuated nodes in AZ-3, rebalanced capacity

Final technical note for the thread — timeline and actions taken:
- 09:00 UTC: CloudFin reports spike in 5xx and latency from AZ-3
- 09:24 UTC: Router weight override + eastus fallback enabled (diversion enacted)
- 09:30–10:15 UTC: Telemetry collection and kernel log analysis (evidence of TX timeouts tied to a recent kernel patch on a subset of nodes)
- 11:00 UTC: Marked affected instances as draining and redirected new allocations to healthy hosts
- 12:10 UTC: Completed instance replacement and verified model-serving process health
- 13:40 UTC: Gradually restored AZ-3 weight to 50% after validation; monitoring continues

Root cause: regression introduced by a host kernel upgrade that triggered sporadic transmit timeouts on a small percentage of instances in AZ-3, which produced amplified retries and error surface.

Mitigations & follow-ups:
- Reverted the kernel patch for the affected host image; pipeline patch hold until full QA signoff (INF-7231)
- Added an automated guard in our deployment pipeline to block kernel rollouts without a critical-path perf canary for serving nodes
- Runbook updated with an explicit AZ-level diversion checklist and rollback steps (attached)
- Post-incident summary and timeline to be published to CloudFin and internal stakeholders by 17:00 UTC

Please let me know if CloudFin wants a joint postmortem meeting.

Karthik
SRE — Serving Runtime
